lines.note: Cajeno yamai identifies an illness attributed to wind; the Portuguese begins the same explanation. The second native pass resolves a caron, not a tilde, over u. The supplied NINJAL Entry Words Data of Nippojisho (v202510, Hideyuki Ohshima with Taichi Aida, CC BY 4.0; https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html) independently corroborates the lexical identity, not the scan typography.
Completes the preceding definition, an illness proceeding from wind. This is a continuation, not a separate headword or an instruction about weather.
Fubo denotes father and mother, individually glossed chichi and faua. Preserve the historical f spelling and Portuguese Pay and nasalized mãy.
Vqiqi identifies floating wood; the Portuguese describes a piece of wood moving on water. The initial V is the positional spelling of u, not a different Japanese consonant.
The example compares the event to a blind turtle encountering floating wood. Ayeru is the historical encounter form; the complete Japanese example remains roman.

runs.text: Como tartaruga cega que encontra com algum

lines.note: The Portuguese explicitly identifies the blind turtle and its encounter, supporting Mǒqi in the Japanese example. Restore the visibly capitalized Como and continue the sentence below.
Completes the turtle's encounter with a piece of wood in water. The sparse short line is intentional; no additional body text is visible to its right.
Vocaſazu expresses not violating, and the Portuguese interprets the entry as chastity. The paragraph begins a Fubon no guiǒ example continued on the next row.

The example means to perform the practice of chastity; the Portuguese speaks of mortifying the flesh while keeping chastity. The visible terminal mark divides guar-dando, not a sentence-ending period.
Completes guardando castidade across the physical break. The draft's dar do is a misdivision; the letters form dando, the gerund required by the preceding guar-.
The term denotes a small bag for letters. Keep the diminutive Saquinho and the manuscript's unaccented cartas rather than expanding the definition.

Xejono sata is public talk or rumour. The second pass retains the aligned draft rumer provisionally: rumor is semantically expected, but the damaged round letter appears e-like. Preserve q̃; do not silently normalize a possible printing anomaly.
The report circulates among the people; Fǔbun suru is then illustrated by the corresponding verbal expression. The accented u is worn but visible in this repetition.
Completes the verbal definition, for a report or reputation to circulate. This short continuation belongs to Fǔbun suru, not the following snowstorm entry.
The verb describes wind blowing with snow; u and uita are the dictionary's abbreviated inflected forms. Preserve neue and the historical past-form presentation.
The noun denotes the wind blowing during snowfall. Correct Fobuqi to the visible Fubuqi; the example's initial Fu is printed at the right edge without a securely visible hyphen.

The alternatives describe being blown on by, or meeting, a snowstorm. Restore the Portuguese Encõ- from the surviving E and the continuation -trar; retain both Japanese alternatives and the caron in vǒ.
Completes encontrar com este vento, then supplies the expression Fubuqiga suru. The final Japanese verb is suru, with long ſ in the printed roman text.
The definition combines blowing wind and falling snow. Chouer neue is the historical Portuguese wording; do not replace it with a modern meteorological expression.
Fubuqidauore is falling when caught in the snow-bearing wind. The following row completes the definition and repeats the headword in an example.
The example is meeting with a blizzard-induced fall; the ending is dauoreni, not the draft's dauoroni. The final abbreviated Idẽ refers back to the same meaning.

runs.text: Não ſer bom, ou não cõ

lines.note: This Fuca means not good or unsuitable, as Yocarazu explains. The Portuguese cõ continues as uir without a printed hyphen; it does not belong to the following shark headword.
Completes the Portuguese verb convir across the unhyphenated break. The separate S. is the dictionary's written-language label and is retained outside the italic definition.
This distinct homonym names a shark. The worn internal e of Peixe has sufficient residual ink; no biological name or modern spelling is added.
Fucaberi describes a broad edging, here applied to tatami or mushiro. Preserve the unhyphenated physical split mu/xiro and the printed alternative marker l,.

runs.text: Certa laya de Tatamis, ou eſteiras que

lines.note: Completes muxiro and begins the Portuguese explanation of a kind of mat. Tatamis is a Japanese-derived term embedded in Portuguese prose, so it is separately flagged for whole-word font review.

runs.text: tem o debrum, ou bainha ao derredor larga.

lines.note: The mats have broad binding or a broad hem around their edges. Restore the visible i and word boundary in bainha ao; the draft's banhaao does not represent these letters.
The adverb means deeply or intimately. The grammatical label appears as Aduero.; retain that abbreviated or anomalous printed form rather than silently expanding it to adverbio.
Completes the second Portuguese adverb, intimately. Correct the draft's imtimamente to the visible n before t; this gloss belongs to Fucabucato.
The adjective denotes something deep or profound. Its final ij and the following derived forms are historical spellings, not errors to be normalized to modern Japanese.
This indented derivative is the abstract -sa form of the preceding adjective, denoting depth or profundity. No separate Portuguese definition is printed on this row.
This indented contracted form belongs to the preceding adjective's paradigm. Preserve the visible caron and its existing indentation rather than treating it as an independent entry.
Here Fucacu is disgrace or a mishap through insufficient preparation, not the adverb meaning deeply. Infamia has f, and the definition distinguishes dishonour and disaster.
The definition attributes the mishap to not preparing beforehand. Restore the omitted same-row paragraph and Fucacuuo, which begins the example continued by caqu below; no new line ID is needed.

runs.text: Infamarſe, ou ficar leſo, ou com al-

lines.note: Completes Fucacuuo caqu, incurring disgrace or a mishap. The Portuguese explains becoming dishonoured or harmed, with the terminal hyphen dividing al-gum.
Completes algum desastre and closes the example with et cetera. Preserve the physical hyphenation across the preceding row and the long-s forms visible here.
Fucacujin is a person who acts without sufficient consideration or makes an error. Restore the joined inconſiderada and retain the printed double-s ligature in Peßoa.

runs.text: ou lhe aconteceo algum deſaſtre por pouco apa-

lines.note: The definition also covers someone suffering a mishap for lack of preparation. Preserve the old aconteceo and the physical division apa-relho.
Completes apparelho in its preparation/equipment sense and offers lack of consideration as the other cause. This closes Fucacujin rather than defining the following footwear.
The footwear term is explained as shoes resembling boots. The historical tç spelling belongs to the Japanese headword; the Portuguese uses the cedilla in Calçado.

runs.text: Couſa profunda, ou de muito fundo.

lines.note: The adjective means deep or having considerable depth. Correct Conſa to Couſa, whose u is visible; the following paragraph extends the sense beyond physical depth.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Couſa grande, in ſpiritualibus, co-

lines.note: Adds a figurative sense of greatness in spiritual or nonphysical matters. The Latin phrase remains within the printed italic passage, and co- continues as como below.
Examples of this figurative depth include knowledge, virtue and benefit. Preserve the unaccented historical forms and the continuation of co-mo across the line break.
The indented -sa derivative denotes depth, following Fucai. The apparent l-like letter is the long ſ used in this suffix, not a separate lexical stem.
The indented contracted form belongs to the Fucai paradigm. Its visible downward-pointing diacritic is a caron, retained rather than replaced by a circumflex.

runs.text: O entrar, ou meterſe muito pellos

lines.note: Fucairi denotes entering deeply or penetrating far, here into the enemy's ranks. Preserve the historical doubled l in pellos and the continuation on the following physical row.

The example is penetrating deeply into the enemy's position; the scan reads fucairiuo, not fucamiuo. A separate printed Idem row follows but has no supplied stable ID; its insertion is reported separately.
Idem refers the preceding Teqiginni fucairiuo suru example back to penetrating deeply into the enemy position. This final physical body row was absent from the draft.

runs.text: Pègo, ou lugar muito fundo no rio,

lines.note: Fucami is a deep place in water, here a deep pool in a river. The Portuguese Pègo bears the visible accent, and the definition continues with the sea alternative below.
The alternative marker extends the preceding definition to a deep place in the sea. This short italic continuation is not a separate Japanese synonym.
The long-vowel headword combines wind and cold. Its caron distinguishes it from the following unaccented Fucan, which has an unrelated meaning.

runs.text: Ignorancia, ou pouco ſaber em algũa

lines.note: This Fucan means ignorance or limited knowledge of something. Preserve the nasal abbreviation in algũa; the last noun is supplied on the next physical row.
Completes the object of limited knowledge, some thing or matter. The short row closes Fucan before the corresponding adjectival entry.

runs.text: Peſſoa ignorante, ou que não ſabe

lines.note: The adjectival form characterizes an ignorant or unknowledgeable person. Two long-s ascenders are visible in Peſſoa, correcting the draft's single-s reading.
Completes the description of a person not knowing something well. Keep the nasalized algũa and the physical separation from Fucanna's first row.

runs.text: Lugar fundo, ou pègo do mar.

lines.note: Fucari denotes a deep place or pool in the sea. The Portuguese reinforces the depth vocabulary in neighboring entries without licensing a change to the Japanese headword.

The Japanese term concerns deep, boggy fields; the Portuguese refers to marshy ground. The visible spacing is da toleiro, an anomalous division related to atoleiro, retained instead of silently respelling it.
Vbecatazu explains what cannot be apprehended; the Portuguese says not to be understood. This is an inability-to-grasp expression, not an imperative telling the reader not to understand.

Completes the definition with inability to perceive well. The label is Bup., with a descended p rather than the draft's o, identifying Buddhist usage. The italic appearance here is retained; the later Bup. at c2-l019 is roman.
Toqu becarazu explains something that cannot be expounded or stated. The headword ends in t, not the draft's added i, and the Portuguese ex- continues below.
Completes explicar and introduces a combined example using Fucatocu and Fucaxet. Preserve the explicit hyphen in fuca- rather than joining the two physical lines.

The combined expression describes a matter or principle beyond understanding and explanation. Cotouari is restored from the worn internal position and the Japanese kotowari context; the a remains graphically weak and is flagged.
Completes the paired negative definition: neither adequately understood nor explained. Both verbs correspond to the two Japanese terms in the preceding example.
The term describes something profound and lofty or beyond ordinary comprehension. Preserve the historical x spelling and the Portuguese wording rather than substituting a modern dictionary gloss.
The -na and -no forms are offered as alternatives with the same meaning. They form their own Japanese lexical row and are not embedded Portuguese typeface terms.
The example combines not knowing with lack of awareness. The worn middle letters support fucaqu rather than fueaqu; the descended q before u is retained as printed.
Completes the lack of reasoning or reflection in the Fuchi fucaqu example. The final Bup. labels Buddhist usage; it is not part of the Japanese phrase.
This homonym means payment or a stipend. The example begins Fuchiuo suru, divided by a printed hyphen after ſu-; retain the grave accent in Pàga.

runs.text: Pagar à gente que hum tem à ſua conta,

lines.note: Completes suru and explains paying the people maintained at one's expense. Preserve hum and the two grave-accented à forms visible in the Portuguese.
The alternative verb means supporting or maintaining those people. It closes the stipend entry, not the next river-pool homonym.
This Fuchi is a deep pool in a river. Pego is unaccented in this occurrence; do not copy the accent from the earlier Pègo entries.

runs.text: Hum ferro que cinge a Catana entre o

lines.note: The term names an iron fitting encircling a sword near its handle. Catana is embedded in the Portuguese explanation and is flagged for whole-word typeface review.
Completes the location of the metal fitting with the printed terms punho and cabos. Preserve this historical description rather than replacing it with modern sword-part terminology.

runs.text: Faſquias, ou paos ſemelhantes que po-

lines.note: This homonym denotes battens or similar pieces of wood used as edging. The physical hyphen divides po-em; it is not a missing nasal sign to be supplied editorially.

runs.text: em no bocal, ou borda dalgũa couſa. ¶

lines.note: Completes the placement around an opening or rim and begins a Japanese example. Preserve the nasal mark in dalgũa and the explicit Fu- break.
The alternatives mean attaching or making the edging. The initial V in vtçu and the tç cluster are historical Japanese spellings; the Portuguese faſqui- continues below.
Completes faſquias and the alternative paos, the wooden strips just described. This is the conclusion of the construction example, not a new lexical item.
Fuchiannai is glossed by Buannai and describes someone unfamiliar with a place or business. Buannai follows i, as a Japanese synonym, so it is not flagged as embedded Portuguese.

runs.text: algũa terra, caſa, ou em algum negocio. &c.

lines.note: Lists a locality, household or undertaking in which the person is new. The Portuguese spelling negocio is unaccented and its following punctuation is retained.

runs.text: Certa laya de caixas quadradas em

lines.note: The headword names a kind of square box or tray. Join the draft's false internal space in quadradas; the definition continues with what is carried in the boxes.

runs.text: que trazem a fruta de ſobre meſa.

lines.note: The boxes carry fruit served after a meal. The scan reads fruta, with no n; preserve the historical separate words ſobre meſa.
Chiguiǒ xezu means not holding the income or land concerned. The Portuguese confirms the lack of revenue; no terminal period is securely printed after renda on this row.
The example explains losing or not possessing such revenue or holdings. The entire row, including its separately detected paragraph sign, is included in the corrected crop.
Completes the objects of losing or lacking: revenue or lands. The short continuation closes Fuchiguiǒ before the following entry on changing fortunes.
Vqi and xizzumu are floating and sinking; the Portuguese develops their figurative sense as hardship. Preserve the doubled z of the historical Japanese form.

runs.text: tribulação como quem anda às voltas com as

lines.note: The definition compares tribulation to being tossed about among waves. The accent in às and the connection with the floating/sinking gloss are retained.

runs.text: ondas, ora em baixo, ora em cima. ¶ Itẽ,

lines.note: Completes the wave comparison, now below and now above. Correct baico to the visible baixo; the following paragraph begins a further sense of the same term.
The further sense is a lord's disfavour, illustrated by Fuchin suru. The scan has u, not o, in the verb, matching the Japanese construction.

A distinct pulse sense is introduced here: an alert or perceptible pulse, contrasted below with a sunken one. Eſperto has no extra i; this physical row needed an independently located crop because the saved detections omitted it.
Fumiacu supplies the floating-pulse synonym; the Portuguese then identifies the sunken pulse as Chinmiacu. Restore the l in Pulſo and mi in Chinmiacu; only Chinmiacu is embedded in Portuguese prose.

runs.text: Lugar fundo, baixo, ou de pouca

lines.note: Fuchixe combines deep-pool and shoal vocabulary; the printed Portuguese juxtaposes fundo and baixo before little water. Preserve that wording rather than harmonizing the apparent deep/shallow tension.
Completes de pouca agua, a place with little water. The noun is unaccented in the scan and is not to be modernized to água.
Fuchǔ is being within the principal town of a regional polity. Preserve the final long-vowel caron and continue the territorial description on the next row.

The principal town belongs to a particular kingdom or province; the paragraph then introduces a second sense. Prouincia restores the missing r and the worn positional u of the draft's malformed Poaincia.
The second sense is the principal town itself. Retain the tightly printed Ameſma and the long ſ instead of normalizing the phrase's spacing and spelling.
